open_points.subject: Contract activation after the trial corpus grows
open_points.text: M06 says a trial case is an input set “that every implementation of a contract version must pass”; M08 says activation “requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus”; but M09 has no transition when a case is added, and M19 starts a run from the contract version's current activation.
open_points.question: When adding or capturing a trial case changes the corpus, what happens to an existing activation whose admission covered the previous corpus, and may new runs still pin it?
options: The activation remains current and usable until another implementation is admitted or rolled back.
The activation record remains, but it becomes ineligible for new runs until its implementation is admitted over the new corpus.
Adding the case automatically reruns admission for the active implementation and either preserves or removes its current usability.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the activation record but refuse new runs that would use it until the implementation is admitted over the new corpus; already-started runs keep their pin.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution identity
open_points.text: M23 declares `### Identity` as `value`, but its identity evidence says “an attempt's record is issued once”; M07 describes execution observations issued once as entities because repeated observations can have equal facts.
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution a value identified by all of its facts, or an entity minted for the attempt and identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)` or by a separate identifier?
options: A value; equal complete records are interchangeable.
An entity identified by the attempt tuple `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`.
An entity with a separately minted NodeExecution identifier.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by the attempt tuple, without adding a random identifier.

open_points.subject: Terminal run transitions with outstanding sends
open_points.text: The cancel action says “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent”, and refusing an effect ends the run `refused`, while M19 permits independent branches to keep running and M26 permits an EffectAttempt to be `in_flight`.
open_points.question: What happens to already-running node executions and already-sent `in_flight` effects when another action makes the run `cancelled` or `refused`, including whether their later responses may update NodeExecution and EffectAttempt records?
options: Let already-sent work conclude and record its observed outcome, but never advance the graph or send anything else.
Immediately convert outstanding work to a terminal failure or `unknown` record and ignore later responses.
Delay the run's terminal transition until all already-started work concludes.
Disallow cancellation or refusal while any other node or effect is in flight.
open_points.default_guess: End the run immediately, send nothing new, but continue recording the eventual outcome of work already sent without advancing the graph.

open_points.subject: Guards sourced from mapped nodes
open_points.text: M14 says that for a mapped node “each output collects one result per element in that order”, while M15 allows a guard to name “an output port of the same source node” and enables an edge when “that port's value equals” one closed-set member.
open_points.question: May a guarded edge originate from a mapped node, and if so is its guard evaluated separately for each mapped element or once against the collected output?
options: The guard is evaluated per mapped element and filters delivery element by element.
The guard is evaluated once against the collected output value.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse guarded edges whose source node is mapped until element-wise guard semantics are explicitly defined.
